subject: Zephyr pilot capacity: activation playbook and tri-region sizing
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@zephyr.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@zephyr.ai>, CloudOps Partner <cloudops@partnercloud.co>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot capacity ask - tri-region baseline

Hey David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to start a 6-week pilot with Redwood for our inference stack and need a quick sketch of what tri-region dedicated capacity would look like (US primary, EU failover, APAC low-latency pilot). High level requirements from our side:~
- Peak concurrent sustained qps equivalent to ~120 token-generation vms (~20k tokens/minute)
- Warm standby in EU for DR, cold burst in APAC for peak hours (initially 30% of US sustained)
- Data residency for EU (logs + KV cache metadata)

Can you send an activation playbook + rough SKU/estimate so we can scope internal approvals? We have an internal security review starting Apr 25 so any compliance/RPO notes are helpful.

Attached: small CSV with traffic samples (sent separately via Drive).

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Lead ML Platform Engineer, Zephyr Systems
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@zephyr.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask - tri-region baseline

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a compact activation playbook and a tri-region sizing memo by EOD Monday. Quick notes up front so expectations align:~
- We'll propose a US baseline pool sized for the sustained qps + 20% safety margin, an EU warm-standby with KV/log geo-fencing, and an APAC pilot pool at ~30% capacity with burst lanes.
- Billing model for pilot: reserved commit for baseline + burst metered on usage; we can show a blended unit cost in the spreadsheet.
- Compliance: EU-only logs and KV can be configured in a Private control plane; I'll flag what requires Private vs Dedicated.

Irene — can you run a 3-sku sizing (g4dn-like, a40-like quantized, and 8-bit quant) for Zephyr's workload profile? Hannah — can you add a short ops runbook for activation + failover gates? Priyom — please draft a short SOW outline we can share with Alex.

I'll consolidate and send the draft playbook + estimate.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Head of Capacity & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot capacity ask - tri-region baseline

Quick sizing notes after a first pass on Alex's sample traffic (attached in Drive link):

Summary (ballpark):
- US baseline pool: 16 x A40-quant nodes (sustained throughput target), continuous batching + 512-token avg => estimated stable throughput ~ 18k tokens/min across pool.
- EU warm-standby: 6 x A40-quant nodes (KV fenced, no shared logs), kept warm with low-traffic heartbeats; automatic failover policy + pre-warmed KV snapshots.
- APAC pilot pool (SG): 5 x g4dn-equivalent nodes (lower-memory quantized runtime) for low-latency bursts, with automatic scale-to-zero for off-hours.

Alternative cost-saving option: move APAC to a mixed-quant profile (8-bit) — reduces node count to 3 but increases risk of marginal quality regression on long-context prompts (we should flag in playbook).

I'll attach a short spreadsheet of SKU math (zephyr_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a note on cache-locality implications for EU-only residency.

-Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: zephyr_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 82KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot capacity ask - tri-region baseline

Folks — ops notes to include in the activation playbook:~
- Activation gates: model pinned version + smoke-test prompts, synthetic load ramp (0 -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 24h), KV consistency check across regions.
- Failover policy: EU takeover only for read-only inference; write operations (KV updates) require manual confirmation for first 48h.
- Runbook checklist items for CS/Dev: API key scoping, per-route cost caps, alerting on token burn rate exceeding 1.25x expected.
- Rollback plan: immediate route revert to hosted fallback model variant if latency > 3x baseline during rollout.

I'll draft the ops section into the playbook doc. Also propose a 2-hour kickoff with Zephyr ops (Alex + Maria) to walk the playbook pre-activation.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: zephyr_activation_playbook_draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@zephyr.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, CloudOps Partner <cloudops@partnercloud.co>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask - tri-region baseline

Alex / Maria — attaching our draft activation playbook and capacity estimate for the 6-week pilot. Key callouts up front:~

1) Recommended baseline & pricing
- US baseline: 16 quantized A40-equivalent nodes (reserved commit) — covers sustained workload + 20% buffer.
- EU warm-standby: 6 nodes, geo-fenced KV and log retention in EU-only cluster.
- APAC pilot: 5 g4dn-like nodes (scale-to-zero) — we also provide an option at 3 nodes using 8-bit quant (cheaper, small quality risk).

2) Operational gates & playbook highlights
- We propose a 2-hour kickoff this Thursday (Apr 17) to review activation steps and assign runbook roles.
- Failover mode limits write-heavy KV ops for first 48 hours; we'll run a dry failover test in the EU warm cluster during week 2 of pilot.

3) Procurement & SOW
- For the pilot we expect a 6-week reserved commit for the US baseline, billed monthly, with burst metering for APAC and any overage in EU. Priyom attached a one-page SOW outline for internal approvals.

Attachments: zephyr_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx, zephyr_activation_playbook_draft.docx, sow_outline.pdf

Next steps: confirm kickoff time and whether Zephyr prefers the APAC pilot in Singapore or Tokyo (we have slightly different latency profiles). Also confirm whether EU log KV must remain in-customer KMS (this affects whether we recommend Private vs Dedicated control plane).

I'll follow up with a HubSpot record and DocuSign-ready SOW once we lock the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

David Kim
Head of Capacity & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
